title.raw: 卷六十一 志第三十七 樂一 Volume 61 Treatises 37: Music 1

sentences.zh: 志第三十七 樂一

translations.literal: Treatise 37, Music 1
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 37: Music, Part One

sentences.zh: 古先聖王，治定功成而作樂，以合天地之性，類萬物之情，天神格而民志協。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings, when governance was settled and achievements accomplished, then composed music, to harmonize with the nature of Heaven and Earth, classify the sentiments of the ten thousand things, cause the spirits of Heaven to descend, and align the wills of the people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the sage kings, once order was secured and their work complete, composed music to accord with the nature of Heaven and Earth, give form to the feelings of all things, draw down the heavenly spirits, and bring the people's hearts into harmony.

sentences.zh: 蓋樂者心聲也，君心和，六合之內無不和矣。

translations.literal: For music is the voice of the heart; when the ruler's heart is harmonious, within the six directions there is nothing not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Music is the outward expression of the heart: when the ruler's heart is at peace, harmony prevails throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 是以樂作於上，民化於下。

translations.literal: Therefore music is performed above, and the people are transformed below.
translations.idiomatic: Thus music issued from above would transform the people below.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢而降，斯理浸微，聲音之道與政治不相通，而民之風俗日趨於靡曼。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, this principle gradually declined; the way of sound did not connect with government, and the people's customs daily tended toward dissipation and softness.
translations.idiomatic: From the Qin and Han dynasties onward this principle faded; music no longer spoke to politics, and popular taste drifted ever further toward the frivolous and ornate.

sentences.zh: 明興，太祖銳志雅樂。

translations.literal: When the Ming arose, the founding emperor was keenly intent on elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming dynasty rose, the Hongwu Emperor was determined to restore proper court music.

sentences.zh: 是時，儒臣冷謙、陶凱、詹同、宋濂、樂韶鳳輩皆知聲律，相與究切釐定。

translations.literal: At that time, the Confucian officials Leng Qian, Tao Kai, Zhan Tong, Song Lian, Yue Shaofeng and the like all understood pitch and mode, and together pursued careful examination and correction.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars such as Leng Qian, Tao Kai, Zhan Tong, Song Lian, and Yue Shaofeng all knew music theory and worked together to investigate and fix the standards.

sentences.zh: 而掌故闊略，欲還古音，其道無由。

translations.literal: But the institutional records were broad and sketchy; wishing to return to ancient tones, they had no way to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the surviving regulations were vague and incomplete, so the path back to ancient pitch was blocked.

sentences.zh: 太祖亦方以下情偷薄，務嚴刑以束之，其於履中蹈和之本，未暇及也。

translations.literal: The founding emperor was also just then, because popular sentiment was lax and shallow, devoting himself to severe punishments to restrain it; as to the root of treading the center and practicing harmony, he had no leisure to attend to it.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was also occupied at the time with tightening lax morals through harsh law and had little leisure for the deeper work of cultivating harmony.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝訪問黃鐘之律，臣工無能應者。

translations.literal: The Wen Emperor inquired about the pitch of the yellow bell; among the officials none could answer.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor asked about the yellow-bell pitch, not one minister could reply.

sentences.zh: 英、景、憲、孝之世，宮縣徒爲具文。

translations.literal: In the reigns of Ying, Jing, Xian, and Xiao, the palace ensembles were merely empty forms on paper.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ying, Jing, Xian, and Xiaozong emperors the court orchestras existed only as empty formalities.

sentences.zh: 殿廷燕享，郊壇祭祀，教坊羽流，慢瀆苟簡，劉翔、胡瑞爲之深慨。

translations.literal: At palace banquets and suburban altar sacrifices, the musicians of the Instruction Office were irreverent, careless, and perfunctory; Liu Xiang and Hu Rui deeply lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: At court feasts and suburban sacrifices the Instruction Office musicians performed with casual irreverence, to the deep distress of Liu Xiang and Hu Rui.

sentences.zh: 世宗製作自任，張鶚、李文察以審音受知，終以無成。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor took creative responsibility upon himself; Zhang E and Li Wenchao gained favor for examining pitch, yet in the end achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor took music reform upon himself and favored Zhang E and Li Wenchao for their expertise in pitch, yet nothing lasting came of it.

sentences.zh: 蓋學士大夫之著述止能論其理，而施諸五音六律輒多未協，樂官能紀其鏗鏘鼓舞而不曉其義，是以卒世莫能明也。

translations.literal: For the writings of scholar-officials could only discuss the principle, yet when applied to the five tones and six modes many points did not agree; music officers could record the clangor and drumming but did not understand the meaning—thus to the end of the age none could make it clear.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials could discuss theory but rarely matched the five tones and six modes in practice; music officers could notate performances without grasping their meaning—so the system was never truly understood.

sentences.zh: 稽明代之製作，大抵集漢、唐、宋、元人之舊，而稍更易其名。

translations.literal: Examining the Ming dynasty's productions, they largely gathered the old of Han, Tang, Song, and Yuan people, and slightly changed their names.
translations.idiomatic: Ming musical arrangements drew chiefly on Han, Tang, Song, and Yuan precedents with only minor renaming.

sentences.zh: 凡聲容之次第，器數之繁縟，在當日非不爛然俱舉，第雅俗雜出，無從正之。

translations.literal: As for the sequence of sound and appearance, the complexity of instruments and numbers—in their day these were not failing to be fully displayed, only elegant and vulgar mixed together with no means to correct them.
translations.idiomatic: The order of performances and the profusion of instruments were fully displayed in their day, yet refined and vulgar elements mingled with no way to sort them out.

sentences.zh: 故備列於篇，以資考者。

translations.literal: Therefore they are fully listed in this treatise, to supply material for investigators.
translations.idiomatic: They are therefore set out here in full for later reference.

sentences.zh: 太祖初克金陵，即立典樂官。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor first took Jinling, he immediately established officials for canonical music.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the Hongwu Emperor captured Jinling he established a bureau for court music.

sentences.zh: 其明年置雅樂，以供郊社之祭。

translations.literal: The next year he established elegant music to supply the suburban and altar sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he instituted ceremonial music for suburban and state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吳元年，命自今朝賀，不用女樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wu, he ordered that from this day forward court congratulations were not to use female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Wu regime he decreed that court congratulations would no longer employ female musicians.

sentences.zh: 先是命選道童充樂舞生，至是始集。

translations.literal: Earlier he had ordered that Daoist youths be selected to serve as music and dance students; only now did they assemble.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier ordered Daoist youths chosen as music and dance trainees; they were assembled at this time.

sentences.zh: 太祖御戟門，召學士朱升、范權引樂舞生入見，閱試之。

translations.literal: The founding emperor attended at the Halberd Gate, summoned the academicians Zhu Sheng and Fan Quan to lead the music and dance students in to be seen, and reviewed and tested them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received them at the Halberd Gate, had Zhu Sheng and Fan Quan present the trainees, and examined their performance.

sentences.zh: 太祖親擊石磬，命升辨五音。

translations.literal: The founding emperor personally struck the stone chime and ordered Sheng to distinguish the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself struck the stone chime and asked Zhu Sheng to identify the five tones.

sentences.zh: 升不能審，以宮音爲徵音。

translations.literal: Sheng could not judge correctly and took the gong tone for the zhi tone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sheng could not tell them apart and mistook the gong tone for the zhi.

sentences.zh: 太祖哂其誤，命樂生登歌一曲而罷。

translations.literal: The founding emperor smiled at his error and ordered a music student to ascend and sing one piece, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled at the mistake, had a student perform one ascent song, and dismissed them.

sentences.zh: 是年置太常司，其屬有協律郎等官。

translations.literal: That year the Directorate of the Imperial Clan Sacrifices was established; among its subordinates were the pitch-harmonizing attendant and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was established, with posts including the pitch-regulating attendant.

sentences.zh: 元末有冷謙者，知音，善鼓瑟，以黃冠隱吳山。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan there was Leng Qian, who understood music, was skilled at plucking the se, and as a Daoist recluse hid on Mount Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuan dynasty Leng Qian, a skilled se player who understood music theory, lived in seclusion on Mount Wu as a Daoist.

sentences.zh: 召爲協律郎，令協樂章聲譜，俾樂生習之。

translations.literal: He was summoned as pitch-harmonizing attendant, ordered to harmonize the sound scores of ritual hymns, and made the music students study them.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as pitch-regulating attendant, tasked with harmonizing the scores of ritual hymns for the students to learn.

sentences.zh: 取石靈璧以制磬，採桐梓湖州以制琴瑟。

translations.literal: Stone from Lingbi was taken to make sounding-stones; paulownia and catalpa from Huzhou were gathered to make zithers and se.
translations.idiomatic: Lingbi stone was used for chimes and paulownia and catalpa from Huzhou for zithers and se.

sentences.zh: 乃考正四廟雅樂，命謙較定音律及編鐘、編磬等器，遂定樂舞之制。

translations.literal: Then the elegant music of the four temples was examined and corrected; Qian was ordered to compare and fix pitch and mode and such instruments as the arranged bells and arranged stones, and thereby the system of music and dance was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The music for the four ancestral temples was revised; Leng Qian was ordered to calibrate pitch, modes, and the arranged bells and stones, thus fixing the regulations for music and dance.

sentences.zh: 樂生仍用道童，舞生改用軍民俊秀子弟。

translations.literal: Music students still used Daoist youths; dance students were changed to use outstanding sons of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians continued to be drawn from Daoist youths, but dancers were recruited from promising sons of soldiers and commoners.

sentences.zh: 又置教坊司，掌宴會大樂。

translations.literal: The Instruction Office was also established to manage great music at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The Instruction Office was also established to oversee banquet music.

sentences.zh: 設大使、副使、和聲郎，左、右韶樂，左右司樂，皆以樂工爲之。

translations.literal: There were established chief commissioner, deputy commissioner, harmony voice attendant, left and right Shao music, left and right music directors—all filled by music craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were created for chief and deputy commissioners, harmony directors, left and right Shao music officers, and left and right music supervisors, all filled by professional musicians.

sentences.zh: 後改和聲郎爲奉鑾。

translations.literal: Later the harmony voice attendant was changed to bell-bearer.
translations.idiomatic: The post of harmony director was later renamed bell-bearer.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年春，親祭太社、太稷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Hongwu, he personally sacrificed to the Great Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1368 the emperor personally sacrificed at the altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 夏祫享於太廟。

translations.literal: In summer he performed the he sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he offered the he sacrifice at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 其冬祀昊天上帝於圜丘。

translations.literal: That winter he sacrificed to the Supreme Lord of the Vast Heavens at the Circular Mound.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he sacrificed to Heaven at the Circular Mound Altar.

sentences.zh: 明年，祀皇地祇於方丘，又以次祀先農、日月、太歲、風雷、嶽瀆、周天星辰、歷代帝王、至聖文宣王，皆定樂舞之數，奏曲之名。

translations.literal: The next year he sacrificed to the Imperial Earth Spirit at the Square Mound, and in sequence also sacrificed to the Spirit of Agriculture, sun and moon, Grand Year, wind and thunder, mountains and rivers, all the stars of heaven, successive dynastic emperors, and the Ultimate Sage King of Culture—fixing in each case the numbers of music and dance and the names of the pieces performed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sacrificed to Earth at the Square Mound and in turn established rites for Agriculture, the sun and moon, the Grand Year star, wind and thunder, mountains and rivers, the stars of heaven, past emperors, and Confucius, fixing for each the number of dancers and musicians and the names of the pieces.

translations.idiomatic: At the Circular Mound: for welcoming the spirit, *Harmonizing the Center* was performed.

translations.idiomatic: For presenting jade and silks, *Solemn Harmony* was performed.

translations.idiomatic: The Square Mound rite followed the same order with different lyrics; the burning-watch piece was replaced by a burial-watch piece.

translations.idiomatic: For the Soil and Grain altars the welcoming piece became *Broad Harmony*, the victim presentation was omitted, and the remainder matched the Square Mound sequence with its own lyrics.

translations.idiomatic: For the Spirit of Agriculture: welcoming the spirit and presenting silks, *Everlasting Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 初獻，奏《壽和之曲》了認識的辯證法，物質的運動形式以及自然科學的分類原則，《武功之舞》。

translations.literal: First offering, perform *Shouhe zhi qu*, with the *Wugong* dance.
translations.idiomatic: For the first offering, *Longevity and Harmony* with the *Martial Merit* dance.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，奏《豫和之曲》，終獻，奏《熙和之曲》，俱《文德之舞》。

translations.literal: Second offering, perform *Yuhe zhi qu*; final offering, perform *Xihe zhi qu*—both with the *Wende* dance.
translations.idiomatic: For the second offering, *Forethought and Harmony*; for the final offering, *Radiant Harmony*—both with the *Civil Virtue* dance.

sentences.zh: 徹豆，奏《雍和之曲》。

translations.literal: Removing the offerings, perform *Yonghe zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For removing the offerings, *Harmonious Peace* was performed.

sentences.zh: 送神，奏《安和之曲》。

translations.literal: Escorting the spirit away, perform *Anhe zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the spirit away, *Secure Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 初獻則德、懿、熙、仁各奏樂舞，亞、終獻則四廟共之。

translations.literal: At the first offering the De, Yi, Xi, and Ren temples each performed their own music and dance; at the second and final offerings the four temples shared them.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the De, Yi, Xi, and Ren shrines had its own music and dance for the first offering; the second and final offerings were shared by all four shrines.

sentences.zh: 釋奠孔子：初用大成登歌舊樂。

translations.literal: Libation sacrifice to Confucius: at first the old music of the Great Completion ascent song was used.
translations.idiomatic: For the Confucius libation rite, the old *Great Completion* ascent music was used at first.

sentences.zh: 洪武六年，始命詹同、樂韶鳳等更制樂章。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, Zhan Tong, Yue Shaofeng, and the like were first ordered to remake the hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1373 Zhan Tong, Yue Shaofeng, and others were ordered to compose new hymn texts.

sentences.zh: 迎神，奏《咸和》。

translations.literal: Welcoming the spirit, perform *Xianhe*.
translations.idiomatic: For welcoming the spirit, *Universal Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 奠帛，奏《寧和》。

translations.literal: Presenting silks, perform *Ninghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting silks, *Tranquil Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 初獻，奏《安和》。

translations.literal: First offering, perform *Anhe*.
translations.idiomatic: For the first offering, *Secure Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻5月。

translations.literal: Second and final offerings both perform *Jinghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For both the second and final offerings, *Serene Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 編入《毛澤東農村調查文集》。

translations.literal: Second and final offerings both perform *Jinghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For both the second and final offerings, *Serene Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 本文批判了王明等人的，奏《景和》。

translations.literal: Both perform *Jinghe*.
translations.idiomatic: Both used *Serene Harmony*.

sentences.zh: 徹饌、送神，奏《咸和》。

translations.literal: Removing the feast and escorting the spirit away, perform *Xianhe*.
translations.idiomatic: For removing the offerings and escorting the spirit away, *Universal Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王：迎神，奏《雍和》。

translations.literal: Successive dynastic emperors: welcoming the spirit, perform *Yonghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For successive dynastic emperors: welcoming the spirit, *Harmonious Peace* was performed.

sentences.zh: 奠帛、初獻，奏《保和》，《武功舞》。

translations.literal: Presenting silks and first offering, perform *Baohe*, with the *Wugong* dance.
translations.idiomatic: For presenting silks and the first offering, *Preserving Harmony* with the *Martial Merit* dance.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，奏《中和》以道爲本，建立道家思想體系。

translations.literal: Second offering, perform *Zhonghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For the second offering, *Harmonizing the Center* was performed.

sentences.zh: 莊子「詆訾孔子之徒，以明，終獻，奏《肅和》，俱《文德舞》。

translations.literal: Final offering, perform *Suhe*—both with the *Wende* dance.
translations.idiomatic: For the final offering, *Solemn Harmony* with the *Civil Virtue* dance.

sentences.zh: 徹豆，奏《凝和》。

translations.literal: Removing the offerings, perform *Ninghe*.
translations.idiomatic: For removing the offerings, *Gathering Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 送神，奏《壽和》。

translations.literal: Escorting the spirit away, perform *Shouhe*.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the spirit away, *Longevity and Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 望瘞，奏《豫和》。

translations.literal: Gazing at the burial, perform *Yuhe*.
translations.idiomatic: For watching the burial of offerings, *Forethought and Harmony* was performed.

sentences.zh: 又定王國祭祀樂章：迎神，奏《太清之曲》。

translations.literal: Regulations were also set for the sacrificial hymns of princely states: welcoming the spirit, perform *Taiqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Princely-state sacrificial hymns were also fixed: for welcoming the spirit, *Supreme Clarity* was performed.

sentences.zh: 初獻，奏《壽清之曲》。

translations.literal: First offering, perform *Shouqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For the first offering, *Clear Longevity* was performed.

sentences.zh: 亞獻，奏《豫清之曲》。

translations.literal: Second offering, perform *Yuqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For the second offering, *Clear Forethought* was performed.

sentences.zh: 終獻，奏《熙清之曲》。

translations.literal: Final offering, perform *Xiqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For the final offering, *Clear Radiance* was performed.

sentences.zh: 徹饌主張社會改良主義。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, perform *Yongqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For removing the offerings, *Clear Harmonious Peace* was performed.

sentences.zh: 在教育學上，認爲教育即生活，學校即社，奏《雍清之曲》。

translations.literal: Removing the feast, perform *Yongqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For removing the offerings, *Clear Harmonious Peace* was performed.

sentences.zh: 送神，奏《安清之曲》。

translations.literal: Escorting the spirit away, perform *Anqing zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the spirit away, *Clear Secure Peace* was performed.

sentences.zh: 其社稷山川，易迎神爲《廣清》，增奉瘞曰《時清》。

translations.literal: For their altars of soil and grain and mountains and rivers, welcoming the spirit was changed to *Guangqing*; presenting for burial was added as *Shiqing*.
translations.idiomatic: For princely altars of Soil and Grain and mountains and rivers, the welcoming piece became *Broad Clarity* and a burial offering piece *Timely Clarity* was added.

sentences.zh: 此祭祀之樂歌節奏也。

translations.literal: These are the rhythms of the sacrificial hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the order of music for these sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，又定朝會宴饗之制。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu, regulations for court assemblies and banquets were also fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1370 regulations for court assemblies and banquets were also established.

sentences.zh: 凡聖節、正旦、冬至、大朝賀，和聲郎陳樂於丹墀百官拜位之南，北向。

translations.literal: For imperial birthdays, New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and great court congratulations, the harmony directors arrayed music south of the officials' bowing positions on the red steps, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial birthdays, New Year's Day, the winter solstice, and major court congratulations, harmony directors placed musicians south of the officials' bowing positions on the red steps, facing north.

sentences.zh: 駕出，仗動。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage emerged, the guard of honor moved.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession emerged, the guard of honor moved.

sentences.zh: 和聲郎舉麾，奏《飛龍引之曲》，樂作，升座。

translations.literal: The harmony directors raised their batons and performed *Feilong yin zhi qu*; music sounded and the emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The harmony directors raised their batons and performed *Leading the Flying Dragon*; music played as the emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 樂止，偃麾。

translations.literal: The music stopped and the batons were lowered.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased and the batons were lowered.

sentences.zh: 百官拜，奏《風雲會之曲》，拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the officials bowed, *Fengyun hui zhi qu* was performed; when the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials bowed, *Gathering of Wind and Clouds* was performed; when the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 丞相上殿致詞，奏《慶皇都之曲》，致詞畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the chief minister ascended to deliver an address, *Qing huangdu zhi qu* was performed; when the address was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister delivered his address, *Celebrating the Imperial Capital* was performed; when the address ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 百官又拜，奏《喜昇平之曲》，拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the officials bowed again, *Xi shengping zhi qu* was performed; when the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials bowed again, *Joy at Ascending Peace* was performed; when the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 駕興，奏《賀聖朝之曲》，還宮，樂止。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage rose, *He shengchao zhi qu* was performed; returning to the palace, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor departed, *Congratulating the Holy Dynasty* was performed; upon return to the palace the music ceased.

sentences.zh: 百官退，和聲郎、樂工以次出。

translations.literal: The officials withdrew, and the harmony directors and musicians left in order.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdrew, and the harmony directors and musicians departed in turn.

sentences.zh: 凡宴饗，和聲郎四人總樂舞，二人執麾，立樂工前之兩旁；

translations.literal: For banquets, four harmony directors supervised music and dance; two held batons and stood on either side before the musicians;
translations.idiomatic: At banquets four harmony directors oversaw music and dance; two held batons on either side before the musicians;

sentences.zh: 二人押樂，立樂工後之兩旁。

translations.literal: two supervised the music and stood on either side behind the musicians.
translations.idiomatic: two supervised the music behind them on either side.

sentences.zh: 殿上陳設畢，和聲郎執麾由兩階升，立於御酒案之左右；

translations.literal: When the hall arrangements were complete, the harmony directors holding batons ascended by the two flights of steps and stood to the left and right of the imperial wine table;
translations.idiomatic: When the hall was set, the baton-holders ascended both stairways and stood beside the imperial wine table;

sentences.zh: 二人引歌工、樂工由兩階升，立於丹陛上之兩旁，東西向。

translations.literal: two others led the singers and musicians up the steps to stand on either side of the red steps, facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: two others led singers and musicians up to stand on either side of the red steps, facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 舞師二人執旌，引武舞士立於西階下之南；

translations.literal: Two dance masters holding banners led martial dancers to stand south of the western steps;
translations.idiomatic: Two dance masters with banners led martial dancers south of the western steps;

sentences.zh: 又二人執翿，引文舞士立於東階下之南；

translations.literal: two others holding feather fans led civil dancers to stand south of the eastern steps;
translations.idiomatic: two with feather fans led civil dancers south of the eastern steps;

sentences.zh: 又二人執幢，引四夷舞士立於武舞之西南；

translations.literal: two others holding streamers led dancers of the four barbarians to stand southwest of the martial dance;
translations.idiomatic: two with streamers led dancers of the four quarters southwest of the martial dancers;

sentences.zh: 俱北向。

translations.literal: all faced north.
translations.idiomatic: all facing north.

sentences.zh: 武舞曰《平定天下之舞》，象以武功定禍亂也；

translations.literal: The martial dance was called *Pingding tianxia zhi wu*, representing settling turmoil by martial achievement;
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance, *Pacifying All Under Heaven*, represented quelling disorder by force of arms;

sentences.zh: 文舞曰《車書會同之舞》，象以文德致太平也；

translations.literal: the civil dance was called *Cheshu huitong zhi wu*, representing bringing great peace through civil virtue;
translations.idiomatic: the civil dance, *Chariots and Documents United*, represented civil virtue bringing universal peace;

sentences.zh: 四夷舞曰《撫安四夷之舞》，象以威德服遠人也。

translations.literal: the dance of the four barbarians was called *Fu'an siyi zhi wu*, representing making distant peoples submit through majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: the dance of the four quarters, *Pacifying the Four Barbarians*, represented winning distant peoples through majesty and virtue.

sentences.zh: 此大樂二人，執戲竹，引大樂工陳列于丹陛之西，文武二舞樂工列于丹陛之東，四夷樂工列於四夷舞之北，俱北向。

translations.literal: Two great-music leaders holding clappers led the great musicians to array west of the red steps; musicians for the civil and martial dances stood east of the red steps; musicians for the four-barbarian dance stood north of that dance—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Two leaders with clappers arrayed the main orchestra west of the red steps; martial and civil musicians stood east; musicians for the four-quarters dance stood north of it—all facing north.

sentences.zh: 駕將出，仗動，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to emerge, the guard moved and great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was about to emerge, the guard moved and the great music began.

sentences.zh: 升座，樂止。

translations.literal: Upon ascending the throne, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he took his seat, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 進第一爵，和聲郎舉麾，唱奏《起臨濠之曲》。

translations.literal: At the first cup, the harmony directors raised their batons and announced *Qi linhao zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: For the first toast the harmony directors raised their batons and announced *Setting Out from Linhao*.

sentences.zh: 引樂二人引歌工、樂工詣酒案前，北面，重行立定。

translations.literal: Two music leaders led singers and musicians before the wine table, facing north, standing in double ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Two leaders brought singers and musicians before the wine table, facing north in double ranks.

sentences.zh: 奏畢，偃麾，押樂引衆工退。

translations.literal: When the performance ended, the batons were lowered and the supervisors led all musicians away.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the batons were lowered and the supervisors led the musicians away.

sentences.zh: 第二，奏《開太平之曲》。

translations.literal: Second, perform *Kai taiping zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Second, *Opening Great Peace*.

sentences.zh: 第三，奏《安建業之曲》。

translations.literal: Third, perform *An jianye zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Third, *Securing Jianye*.

sentences.zh: 第四，奏《大一統之曲》。

translations.literal: Fourth, perform *Da yitong zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, *Great Unity*.

sentences.zh: 第五，奏《平幽都之典》。

translations.literal: Fifth, perform *Ping youdu zhi dian*.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, *Pacifying the Northern Capital*.

sentences.zh: 第六，奏《撫四夷之曲》。

translations.literal: Sixth, perform *Fu siyi zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, *Pacifying the Four Barbarians*.

sentences.zh: 第七，奏《定封賞之曲》。

translations.literal: Seventh, perform *Ding fengshang zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, *Fixing Rewards and Enfeoffments*.

sentences.zh: 第八，奏《大一統之曲》。

translations.literal: Eighth, perform *Da yitong zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, *Great Unity* again.

sentences.zh: 第九，奏《守承平之曲》。

translations.literal: Ninth, perform *Shou chengping zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, *Maintaining Lasting Peace*.

sentences.zh: 其舉麾、偃麾，歌工、樂工進退，皆如前儀。

translations.literal: Raising and lowering the batons and the coming and going of singers and musicians all followed the previous protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Raising and lowering batons and the movements of singers and musicians followed the same protocol throughout.

sentences.zh: 進第一次膳，和聲郎舉麾，唱奏《飛龍引之樂》，大樂作。

translations.literal: At the first serving of food, the harmony directors raised their batons and announced *Feilong yin zhi yue*; great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: At the first course the directors announced *Leading the Flying Dragon* and the great music played.

sentences.zh: 食畢，樂止，偃麾。

translations.literal: When eating was finished, the music stopped and the batons were lowered.
translations.idiomatic: When the meal ended, the music stopped and the batons were lowered.

sentences.zh: 第二，奏《風雲會之樂》。

translations.literal: Second, perform *Fengyun hui zhi yue*.
translations.idiomatic: Second, *Gathering of Wind and Clouds*.

sentences.zh: 第三，奏《慶皇都之樂》。

translations.literal: Third, perform *Qing huangdu zhi yue*.
translations.idiomatic: Third, *Celebrating the Imperial Capital*.

sentences.zh: 第四，奏《平定天下之舞》。

translations.literal: Fourth, perform the *Pingding tianxia* dance.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the *Pacifying All Under Heaven* dance.

sentences.zh: 第五，奏《賀聖朝之樂》。

translations.literal: Fifth, perform *He shengchao zhi yue*.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, *Congratulating the Holy Dynasty*.

sentences.zh: 第六，奏《撫安四夷之舞》。

translations.literal: Sixth, perform the *Fu'an siyi* dance.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, the *Pacifying the Four Barbarians* dance.

sentences.zh: 第七，奏《九重歡之樂》。

translations.literal: Seventh, perform *Jiuchong huan zhi yue*.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, *Joy within the Ninefold Palaces*.

sentences.zh: 第八，奏《車書會同之舞》。

translations.literal: Eighth, perform the *Cheshu huitong* dance.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, the *Chariots and Documents United* dance.

sentences.zh: 第九，奏《萬年春之樂》。

translations.literal: Ninth, perform *Wannian chun zhi yue*.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, *Ten Thousand Years of Spring*.

sentences.zh: 其舉麾、偃麾如前儀。

translations.literal: Raising and lowering the batons followed the previous protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Raising and lowering batons followed the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 九奏三舞既畢，駕興，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the nine performances and three dances were complete, the imperial carriage rose and great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: After the nine performances and three dances, the emperor rose and great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 入宮，樂止，和聲郎執麾引衆工以次出。

translations.literal: Entering the palace, the music stopped; the harmony directors holding batons led all musicians out in order.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering the palace the music ceased; the directors led the musicians out in order.

sentences.zh: 宴饗之曲，後凡再更。

translations.literal: The banquet pieces were later revised twice in all.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet music was later revised twice altogether.

sentences.zh: 四年所定，一曰《本太初》，二曰《仰大明》，三曰《民初生》，四曰《品物亨》，五曰《御六龍》，六曰《泰階平》，七曰《君德成》，八曰《聖道行》，九曰《樂清寧》。

translations.literal: As fixed in the fourth year: first *Ben taichu*, second *Yang daming*, third *Min chusheng*, fourth *Pinwu heng*, fifth *Yu liulong*, sixth *Taijie ping*, seventh *Junde cheng*, eighth *Shengdao xing*, ninth *Yue qingning*.
translations.idiomatic: The 1371 set comprised: *Origin of the Great Beginning*, *Looking Up to Great Brilliance*, *The People First Born*, *All Things Flourishing*, *Driving Six Dragons*, *The Great Steps Level*, *The Ruler's Virtue Complete*, *The Sage Way Advancing*, and *Music Clear and Tranquil*.

sentences.zh: 其詞，詹同、陶凱所制也。

translations.literal: Their texts were composed by Zhan Tong and Tao Kai.
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics were composed by Zhan Tong and Tao Kai.

sentences.zh: 十五年所定，一曰《炎精開運》，二曰《皇風》，三曰《眷皇明》，四曰《天道傳》，五曰《振皇綱》，六曰《金陵》，七曰《長楊》，八曰《芳醴》，九曰《駕六龍》。

translations.literal: As fixed in the fifteenth year: first *Yanjing kaiyun*, second *Huangfeng*, third *Juan huangming*, fourth *Tiandao chuan*, fifth *Zhen huanggang*, sixth *Jinling*, seventh *Changyang*, eighth *Fangli*, ninth *Jia liulong*.
translations.idiomatic: The 1382 set comprised: *Blazing Essence Opens Fortune*, *Imperial Wind*, *Cherishing Imperial Brilliance*, *Heaven's Way Transmitted*, *Shaking the Imperial Net*, *Jinling*, *Long Yang*, *Fragrant Wine*, and *Driving Six Dragons*.

sentences.zh: 凡大朝賀，教坊司設中和韶樂於殿之東西，北向；

translations.literal: For great court congratulations, the Instruction Office set harmonious Shao music east and west of the hall, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: At great court congratulations the Instruction Office placed harmonious Shao music east and west of the hall, facing north;

sentences.zh: 陳大舞于丹陛之東西，亦北向。

translations.literal: great dances were arrayed east and west of the red steps, also facing north.
translations.idiomatic: great dances were arrayed east and west of the red steps, also facing north.

sentences.zh: 駕興，中和韶樂奏《聖安之曲》。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage rose, harmonious Shao music performed *Sheng'an zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rose, harmonious Shao music performed *Holy Peace*.

sentences.zh: 升座進寶，樂止。

translations.literal: Upon ascending the throne and presenting the treasure, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he ascended and the treasure was presented, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 百官拜，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the officials bowed, great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials bowed, great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 進表，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was presented, great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 進訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the presentation was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宣表目，致賀訖，百官俯伏，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the summary of the memorial was announced and congratulations concluded, the officials prostrated themselves and great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial summary was announced and congratulations concluded, the officials prostrated and great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 宣制訖，百官舞蹈山呼，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the edict was announced, the officials danced and shouted *shanhu*; great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was announced, the officials danced and shouted their acclamation; great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 駕興，中和韶樂奏《定安之曲》，導駕至華蓋殿，樂止。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage rose, harmonious Shao music performed *Ding'an zhi qu*, escorting the carriage to the Hall of Imperial Canopy; the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor departed, harmonious Shao music performed *Secure Peace*, escorting him to the Hall of the Imperial Canopy; then the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 百官以次出。

translations.literal: The officials left in order.
translations.idiomatic: The officials withdrew in order.

sentences.zh: 其大宴饗，教坊司設中和韶樂於殿內，設大樂於殿外，立三舞雜隊於殿下。

translations.literal: For great banquets, the Instruction Office set harmonious Shao music inside the hall, great music outside the hall, and established three dances and miscellaneous troupes below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: At great banquets the Instruction Office placed harmonious Shao music inside, great music outside, and arrayed the three dances and miscellaneous troupes below the hall.

sentences.zh: 駕興，大樂作。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage rose, great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rose, great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 升座，樂止。

translations.literal: Upon ascending the throne, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When he took his seat, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 文武官入列於殿外，北向拜，大樂作。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials entered and lined up outside the hall, bowing northward; great music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials lined up outside and bowed northward; great music sounded.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the bowing ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 進御筵，樂作。

translations.literal: When the imperial feast was presented, music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial feast was presented, music sounded.

sentences.zh: 進訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the presentation was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 進花，樂作。

translations.literal: When flowers were presented, music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When flowers were presented, music sounded.

sentences.zh: 進訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the presentation was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the presentation ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 進第一爵，教坊司奏《炎精開運之曲》，樂作。

translations.literal: At the first cup, the Instruction Office performed *Yanjing kaiyun zhi qu*; music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: At the first cup the Instruction Office performed *Blazing Essence Opens Fortune*.

sentences.zh: 內外官拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When inner and outer officials had finished bowing, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When officials within and without had bowed, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 散花，樂作。

translations.literal: When flowers were scattered, music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When flowers were scattered, music sounded.

sentences.zh: 散訖，樂止。

translations.literal: When the scattering was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the scattering ended, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 第二爵，教坊司奏《皇風之曲》。

translations.literal: Second cup: the Instruction Office performed *Huangfeng zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Second cup: the Instruction Office performed *Imperial Wind*.

sentences.zh: 樂止，進湯。

translations.literal: The music stopped and soup was presented.
translations.idiomatic: The music stopped and soup was served.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹饗節前導至殿外，鼓吹止，殿上樂作。

translations.literal: The wind and drum feast procession led forward to outside the hall; the wind drums stopped and hall music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The wind-and-drum procession led to the hall entrance; the wind drums ceased and hall music began.

sentences.zh: 羣臣湯饌成，樂止。

translations.literal: When the ministers' soup and food were ready, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers' soup and dishes were ready, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 武舞入，教坊司請奏《平定天下之舞》。

translations.literal: The martial dance entered; the Instruction Office requested performance of *Pingding tianxia zhi wu*.
translations.idiomatic: The martial dance filed in, and the Instruction Office called for *Pacifying the Realm Under Heaven*.

sentences.zh: 第三爵，教坊司請奏《眷皇明之曲》，進酒如前儀。

translations.literal: Third cup: the Instruction Office requested *Juan huangming zhi qu*; wine was presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the third cup the Instruction Office performed *Cherishing the Bright Ming*; wine was served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，教坊司請奏《撫安四夷之舞》。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the Instruction Office requested *Fu'an siyi zhi wu*.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and the Instruction Office called for *Pacifying the Four Barbarians*.

sentences.zh: 第四爵，奏《天道傳之曲》，進酒進湯如前儀。

translations.literal: Fourth cup: *Tiandao chuan zhi qu* was performed; wine and soup were presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth cup: *Heaven's Way Transmitted*; wine and soup were served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，奏《車書會同之舞》。

translations.literal: The music stopped; *Cheshu huitong zhi wu* was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and *Chariots and Script Unite* was danced.

sentences.zh: 第五爵，奏《振皇綱之曲》，進酒如前儀。

translations.literal: Fifth cup: *Zhen huanggang zhi qu* was performed; wine was presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth cup: *Upholding the Imperial Net*; wine was served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，奏百戲承應。

translations.literal: The music stopped; miscellaneous entertainments were presented.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and variety acts were staged.

sentences.zh: 第六爵，奏《金陵之曲》，進酒進湯如前儀。

translations.literal: Sixth cup: *Jinling zhi qu* was performed; wine and soup were presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth cup: *Jinling*; wine and soup were served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，奏八蠻獻寶承應。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the *Eight Barbarians Presenting Treasures* entertainment was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and the *Eight Barbarians Presenting Treasures* act followed.

sentences.zh: 第七爵，奏《長楊之曲》，進酒如前儀。

translations.literal: Seventh cup: *Changyang zhi qu* was performed; wine was presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh cup: *Long Yang*; wine was served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，奏採蓮隊子承應。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the *Lotus-Picking Lad* entertainment was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and the *Lotus-Picking Lad* act followed.

sentences.zh: 第八爵，奏《芳醴之曲》，進酒進湯如前儀。

translations.literal: Eighth cup: *Fangli zhi qu* was performed; wine and soup were presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth cup: *Fine Mead*; wine and soup were served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，奏魚躍於淵承應。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the *Fish Leaping in the Deep* entertainment was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased, and the *Fish Leaping in the Deep* act followed.

sentences.zh: 第九爵，奏《駕六龍之曲》，進酒如前儀。

translations.literal: Ninth cup: *Jia liu long zhi qu* was performed; wine was presented as before.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth cup: *Driving Six Dragons*; wine was served as before.

sentences.zh: 樂止，收爵。

translations.literal: The music stopped; the cups were collected.
translations.idiomatic: The music ceased and the cups were gathered in.

sentences.zh: 進湯，進大膳，樂作。

translations.literal: Soup was presented, then the great feast; music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Soup and the main banquet were served, and music played.

sentences.zh: 供羣臣飯食訖，樂止，百花隊舞承應。

translations.literal: When the ministers' meal was finished, the music stopped; the Hundred Flowers troupe dance was presented.
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers had eaten, the music stopped and the Hundred Flowers company danced.

sentences.zh: 宴成徹案。

translations.literal: When the feast was complete, the tables were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet ended and the tables were cleared.

sentences.zh: 羣臣出席，北向拜，樂作。

translations.literal: The ministers left their seats and bowed northward; music sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers rose, turned north, and bowed as music played.

sentences.zh: 拜畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, the music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the bows were complete, the music stopped.

sentences.zh: 駕興，大樂作、鳴鞭，百官以次出。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage departed; great music sounded and the whip cracked; officials left in order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's carriage rose; great music and the ceremonial whip sounded, and officials withdrew in turn.

sentences.zh: 此朝賀宴饗之樂歌節奏也。

translations.literal: Such were the rhythms of music and song at court audiences and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the sequence of music and song at audiences and banquets.

sentences.zh: 其樂器之制，郊丘廟社，洪武元年定。

translations.literal: As for the regulations for musical instruments, suburban altars and temples were fixed in Hongwu year 1.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument regulations for suburban altars and temples were set in the first year of Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 樂工六十二人，編鐘、編磬各十六，琴十，瑟四，搏拊四，柷敔各一，壎四，篪四，簫八，笙八，笛四，應鼓一；

translations.literal: Sixty-two musicians; sixteen each of suspended bells and chime-stones, ten zithers, four se, four clappers, one each of sounding-box and wooden tiger, four xun, four chi, eight xiao, eight sheng, four di, and one answering drum;
translations.idiomatic: There were sixty-two musicians: sixteen each of bell-chimes and stone-chimes, ten zithers, four se, four clappers, one sounding-box and one wooden tiger, four xun, four chi, eight xiao, eight sheng, four di, and one answering drum;

sentences.zh: 歌工十二；

translations.literal: twelve singers;
translations.idiomatic: twelve singers;

sentences.zh: 協律郎一從執麾以引之。

translations.literal: one pitch-regulation officer followed, holding the baton to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: and one pitch-regulation officer who followed, baton in hand, to lead them.

sentences.zh: 七年復增籥四，鳳笙四，壎用六，搏拊用二，共七十二人。

translations.literal: In year 7 four yue and four phoenix sheng were added, six xun and two clappers were used, totaling seventy-two persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year four yue and four phoenix sheng were added, xun were increased to six and clappers to two, for seventy-two in all.

sentences.zh: 舞則武舞生六十二人，引舞二人，各執干鏚；

translations.literal: For dance: sixty-two martial dancers, two lead dancers, each holding shield and axe;
translations.idiomatic: For dance there were sixty-two martial dancers and two lead dancers, each with shield and axe;

sentences.zh: 文舞生六十二人，引舞二人，各執羽籥；

translations.literal: sixty-two civil dancers, two lead dancers, each holding plume and flute;
translations.idiomatic: sixty-two civil dancers and two lead dancers, each with plume and reed-pipe;

sentences.zh: 舞師二人執節以引之。

translations.literal: two dance masters held rhythm-sticks to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: and two dance masters with rhythm-sticks to lead them.

sentences.zh: 共一百三十人。

translations.literal: One hundred thirty persons in all.
translations.idiomatic: In all, one hundred thirty persons.

sentences.zh: 惟文廟樂生六十人，編鐘、編磬各十六，琴十，瑟四，搏拊四，柷敔各一，壎四，篪四，簫八，笙八，笛四，大鼓一；

translations.literal: Only at the Confucian temple were sixty music students, with sixteen each of suspended bells and chime-stones, ten zithers, four se, four clappers, one each of sounding-box and wooden tiger, four xun, four chi, eight xiao, eight sheng, four di, and one large drum;
translations.idiomatic: At the Confucian temple alone there were sixty music students, with sixteen each of bell-chimes and stone-chimes, ten zithers, four se, four clappers, one sounding-box and one wooden tiger, four xun, four chi, eight xiao, eight sheng, four di, and one large drum;

sentences.zh: 歌工十。

translations.literal: ten singers.
translations.idiomatic: and ten singers.

sentences.zh: 六年鑄太和鍾。

translations.literal: In year 6 the Great Harmony Bell was cast.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Great Harmony Bell was cast.

sentences.zh: 其制，仿宋景鍾。

translations.literal: Its design followed the Song Jing Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Its design followed the Song dynasty's Jing Bell.

sentences.zh: 以九九爲數，高八尺一寸。

translations.literal: Using nine-times-nine as the measure, it was eight chi and one cun high.
translations.idiomatic: The measure was based on nine nines, and it stood eight chi and one cun tall.

sentences.zh: 拱以九龍，柱以龍虡，建樓於圜丘齋宮之東北，懸之。

translations.literal: Its arch bore nine dragons, its pillars dragon-and-tiger motifs; a tower was built northeast of the Round Mound fasting palace and the bell was suspended there.
translations.idiomatic: Nine dragons arched over it, dragon-and-tiger pillars supported it, and a tower northeast of the Round Mound fasting palace was built to suspend it.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，駕動則鐘聲作。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifice, when the imperial procession moved, the bell sounded.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifice, when the imperial procession set out, the bell sounded.

sentences.zh: 升壇，鍾止，衆音作。

translations.literal: On ascending the altar the bell ceased and all other instruments played.
translations.idiomatic: On mounting the altar the bell stopped and the full ensemble played.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，升輦，鐘聲作。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished and the emperor mounted the palanquin, the bell sounded.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended and the emperor took his palanquin, the bell sounded again.

sentences.zh: 俟導駕樂作，乃止。

translations.literal: It ceased only when the escort music began.
translations.idiomatic: It did not stop until the escort music began.

sentences.zh: 十七年改鑄，減其尺十之四焉。

translations.literal: In year 17 it was recast, reduced in size by four-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year it was recast, its dimensions reduced by four-tenths.

sentences.zh: 朝賀。

translations.literal: Court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年定丹陛大樂：簫四，笙四，箜篌四，方響四，頭管四，龍笛四，琵琶四，闉六，杖鼓二十四，大鼓二，板二。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 3 the cinnabar-steps great music was fixed: four xiao, four sheng, four konghou, four fangxiang, four touguan, four dragon flutes, four pipa, six yu, twenty-four staff-drums, two large drums, and two clappers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 the cinnabar-steps great music was set: four xiao, four sheng, four konghou, four fangxiang, four touguan, four dragon flutes, four pipa, six yu, twenty-four staff-drums, two large drums, and two clappers.

sentences.zh: 二十六年又定殿中韶樂：簫十二，笙十二，排簫四，橫笛十二，壎四，篪四，琴十，瑟四，編鐘二，編磬二，應鼓二，柷一，敔一，捕拊二，丹陛大樂：戲竹二，簫十二，笙十二，笛十二，頭管十二，闉八，琵琶八，二十弦八，方響二，鼓二，拍板八，杖鼓十二。

translations.literal: In year 26 the hall Shao music was also fixed: twelve xiao, twelve sheng, four panpipes, twelve transverse flutes, four xun, four chi, ten zithers, four se, two sets of bell-chimes, two sets of stone-chimes, two answering drums, one sounding-box, one wooden tiger, two clappers; cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, twelve xiao, twelve sheng, twelve di, twelve touguan, eight yu, eight pipa, eight twenty-stringed instruments, two fangxiang, two drums, eight clappers, twelve staff-drums.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 hall Shao music was also fixed: twelve xiao, twelve sheng, four panpipes, twelve transverse flutes, four xun, four chi, ten zithers, four se, two bell-chime sets, two stone-chime sets, two answering drums, one sounding-box, one wooden tiger, two clappers; and cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, twelve xiao, twelve sheng, twelve di, twelve touguan, eight yu, eight pipa, eight twenty-stringed instruments, two fangxiang, two drums, eight clappers, and twelve staff-drums.

sentences.zh: 命婦朝賀中宮，設女樂：戲竹二，簫十四，笙十四，笛十四，頭管十四，闉十，琵琶八，二十弦八，方響六，鼓五，拍板八，杖鼓十二。

translations.literal: When titled ladies attended audience at the inner palace, female music was set: two bamboo conductors, fourteen xiao, fourteen sheng, fourteen di, fourteen touguan, ten yu, eight pipa, eight twenty-stringed instruments, six fangxiang, five drums, eight clappers, twelve staff-drums.
translations.idiomatic: When titled ladies attended the empress at audience, female music was arranged: two bamboo conductors, fourteen xiao, fourteen sheng, fourteen di, fourteen touguan, ten yu, eight pipa, eight twenty-stringed instruments, six fangxiang, five drums, eight clappers, and twelve staff-drums.

sentences.zh: 正旦、冬至、千秋凡三節。

translations.literal: For New Year's Day, Winter Solstice, and Longevity—three festivals in all.
translations.idiomatic: These applied to New Year's Day, the Winter Solstice, and the Longevity festival—three occasions in all.

sentences.zh: 其後太皇太后、皇太后並用之。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager also used them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager used them as well.

sentences.zh: 朔望朝參：戲竹二，簫四，笙四，笛四，頭管四，闉二，琵琶二，二十弦二，方響一，鼓一，拍板二，杖鼓六。

translations.literal: For audience on the first and fifteenth of the month: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, four di, four touguan, two yu, two pipa, two twenty-stringed instruments, one fangxiang, one drum, two clappers, six staff-drums.
translations.idiomatic: For audience on new and full moon: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, four di, four touguan, two yu, two pipa, two twenty-stringed instruments, one fangxiang, one drum, two clappers, and six staff-drums.

sentences.zh: 大宴。

translations.literal: Grand banquets.
translations.idiomatic: Grand banquets.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年定殿內侑食樂：簫六，笙六，歌工四。

translations.literal: In Hongwu year 1 hall-side offering music was fixed: six xiao, six sheng, four singers.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 1 hall-side offering music was set: six xiao, six sheng, and four singers.

sentences.zh: 丹陛大樂：戲竹二，簫四，笙四，琵琶六，闉六，箜篌四，方響四，頭管四，龍笛四，杖鼓二十四，大鼓二，板二。

translations.literal: Cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, six pipa, six yu, four konghou, four fangxiang, four touguan, four dragon flutes, twenty-four staff-drums, two large drums, two clappers.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, six pipa, six yu, four konghou, four fangxiang, four touguan, four dragon flutes, twenty-four staff-drums, two large drums, and two clappers.

sentences.zh: 文武二舞樂器：笙二，橫管二，闉二，杖鼓二，大鼓一，板一。

translations.literal: Civil and martial dance instruments: two sheng, two transverse pipes, two yu, two staff-drums, one large drum, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and martial dance instruments: two sheng, two transverse pipes, two yu, two staff-drums, one large drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 四夷舞樂：腰鼓二，琵琶二，胡琴二，箜篌二，頭管二，羌笛二，闉二，水盞一，板一。

translations.literal: Four-barbarian dance music: two waist-drums, two pipa, two huqin, two konghou, two touguan, two Qiang flutes, two yu, one water-bowl, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Four-barbarian dance music: two waist-drums, two pipa, two huqin, two konghou, two touguan, two Qiang flutes, two yu, one water-bowl, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 二十六年又定殿內侑食樂：祝一，敔一，搏拊一，琴四，瑟二，簫四，笙四，笛四，壎二，篪二，排簫一，鍾一，磬一，應鼓一。

translations.literal: In year 26 hall-side offering music was again fixed: one sounding-box, one wooden tiger, one clapper, four zithers, two se, four xiao, four sheng, four di, two xun, two chi, one panpipe, one bell, one chime-stone, one answering drum.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 hall-side offering music was revised: one sounding-box, one wooden tiger, one clapper, four zithers, two se, four xiao, four sheng, four di, two xun, two chi, one panpipe, one bell, one chime-stone, and one answering drum.

sentences.zh: 丹陛大樂：戲竹二，簫四，笙四，頭管二，琵琶二，闉二，二十弦二，方響二，杖鼓八，鼓一，板一。

translations.literal: Cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, two touguan, two pipa, two yu, two twenty-stringed instruments, two fangxiang, eight staff-drums, one drum, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar-steps great music: two bamboo conductors, four xiao, four sheng, two touguan, two pipa, two yu, two twenty-stringed instruments, two fangxiang, eight staff-drums, one drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 迎膳樂：戲竹二，笙二，笛四，頭管二，闉二，杖鼓十，鼓一，板一。

translations.literal: Welcoming-the-feast music: two bamboo conductors, two sheng, four di, two touguan, two yu, ten staff-drums, one drum, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming-the-feast music: two bamboo conductors, two sheng, four di, two touguan, two yu, ten staff-drums, one drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 進膳樂：笙二，笛二，杖鼓八，鼓一，板一。

translations.literal: Presenting-the-feast music: two sheng, two di, eight staff-drums, one drum, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting-the-feast music: two sheng, two di, eight staff-drums, one drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 太平清樂：笙四，笛四，頭管二，闉四，方響一，杖鼓八，小鼓一，板一。

translations.literal: Great Peace Pure music: four sheng, four di, two touguan, four yu, one fangxiang, eight staff-drums, one small drum, one clapper.
translations.idiomatic: Great Peace Pure music: four sheng, four di, two touguan, four yu, one fangxiang, eight staff-drums, one small drum, and one clapper.

sentences.zh: 樂工舞士服色之制。

translations.literal: Regulations for musicians' and dancers' dress.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for the dress of musicians and dancers.

sentences.zh: 郊廟，洪武元年定；

translations.literal: Suburban temples, fixed in Hongwu year 1;
translations.idiomatic: For suburban temples, fixed in Hongwu year 1;

sentences.zh: 朝賀，洪武三年定。

translations.literal: court audiences, fixed in Hongwu year 3.
translations.idiomatic: for court audiences, fixed in Hongwu year 3.

sentences.zh: 文武兩舞：武舞士三十二人，左幹右戚，四行，行八人，舞作發揚蹈厲坐作擊刺之狀，舞師二人執旌以引之；

translations.literal: Civil and martial dances: thirty-two martial dancers, shield left and axe right, four rows of eight, dancing with vigorous stamping, sitting, thrusting, and striking motions; two dance masters held banners to lead them;
translations.idiomatic: Civil and martial dances: thirty-two martial dancers with shield on the left and axe on the right, four rows of eight, performing vigorous stamping, sitting, thrusting, and striking motions; two dance masters with banners led them;

sentences.zh: 文舞士三十二人，左籥右翟，四行，行八人，舞作進退舒徐揖讓升降之狀，舞師二人執翿以引之。

translations.literal: thirty-two civil dancers, reed-pipe left and pheasant-plume right, four rows of eight, dancing with measured advance and retreat, bowing, yielding, and rising motions; two dance masters held feather-fans to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: thirty-two civil dancers with reed-pipe on the left and pheasant-plume on the right, four rows of eight, performing measured advance, retreat, bowing, yielding, and rising; two dance masters with feather-fans led them.

sentences.zh: 四夷之舞：舞士十六人，四行，行四人，舞作拜跪朝謁喜躍俯伏之狀，舞師二人執幢以引之。

translations.literal: Four-barbarian dance: sixteen dancers, four rows of four, dancing bowing, kneeling, audience, joyful leaping, and prostration; two dance masters held streamers to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Four-barbarian dance: sixteen dancers in four rows of four, performing bows, kneels, audience salutes, joyful leaps, and prostrations; two dance masters with streamers led them.

sentences.zh: 此祭祀朝賀之樂舞器服也。

translations.literal: Such were the music, dance, instruments, and dress for sacrifice and court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the music, dances, instruments, and costumes of sacrifice and court audience.

sentences.zh: 當太祖時，前後稍有增損。

translations.literal: Under the founding emperor there were minor additions and reductions before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Under the founding emperor the regulations were adjusted here and there over time.

sentences.zh: 樂章之鄙者，命儒臣易其詞。

translations.literal: Where hymn texts were vulgar, he ordered Confucian officials to replace the words.
translations.idiomatic: Where hymn texts were crude, he ordered scholar-officials to rewrite them.

sentences.zh: 二郊之作，太祖所親制。

translations.literal: The suburban hymns were personally composed by the founder.
translations.idiomatic: The two suburban hymn cycles were the founder's own work.

sentences.zh: 後改合祀，其詞復更。

translations.literal: Later, when combined sacrifice was adopted, the texts were changed again.
translations.idiomatic: When combined sacrifice was later adopted, the texts were revised again.

sentences.zh: 太社稷奉仁祖配，亦更制七奏。

translations.literal: For the Great Altars of Soil and Grain with the dynastic founder as associate, seven performances were also newly composed.
translations.idiomatic: For the Great Altars of Soil and Grain with the dynastic founder as associate, a new set of seven performances was made.

sentences.zh: 嘗諭禮臣曰：「古樂之詩，章和而正。

translations.literal: He once instructed the ritual officials: "The poetry of ancient music was harmonious in stanza and upright in tone.
translations.idiomatic: He once told the ritual officials: "Poetry in ancient music was harmonious in form and upright in tone.

sentences.zh: 後世之詩，章淫以誇。

translations.literal: The poetry of later ages was dissolute in stanza and boastful.
translations.idiomatic: Later poetry grew dissolute in form and boastful in tone.

sentences.zh: 故一切諛詞豔曲，皆棄不取。

translations.literal: Therefore all flattery, lewd songs, and sensual airs were cast aside and not taken up."
translations.idiomatic: So every flattery, lewd song, and sensual air was rejected."

sentences.zh: 」嘗命儒臣撰迴鑾樂歌，所奏《神降祥》、《神貺》、《酣酒》、《色荒》、《禽荒》諸曲，凡三十九章，命曰《御鑾歌》，皆寓諷諫之意。

translations.literal: He also ordered Confucian officials to compose Returning Palanquin music; pieces such as *Spirit Descends in Blessing*, *Spirit Bestows*, *Deep Drinking*, *Lust for Color*, and *Lust for Birds*—thirty-nine pieces in all—were named *Imperial Palanquin Songs*, all bearing admonitory intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Confucian officials to compose Returning Palanquin songs—*Spirit Descends in Blessing*, *Spirit Bestows*, *Deep Drinking*, *Lust for Color*, *Lust for Birds*, and thirty-four others, thirty-nine in all, titled *Imperial Palanquin Songs*, each meant to admonish.

sentences.zh: 然當時作者，惟務明達易曉，非能如漢、晉間詩歌，鏗鏘雅健，可錄而誦也。

translations.literal: Yet the composers of the day sought only clarity and ease of understanding, and could not match the Han and Jin poetry—sonorous, elegant, and strong enough to be recorded and recited.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who wrote them aimed only at plain clarity, not at the sonorous elegance of Han and Jin verse fit to be sung and remembered.

sentences.zh: 殿中韶樂，其詞出於教坊俳優，多乖雅道。

translations.literal: The Shao music in the hall took its texts from Instruction Office actors and often strayed from the proper way.
translations.idiomatic: Hall Shao music drew its words from Instruction Office performers and often departed from proper taste.

sentences.zh: 十二月樂歌，按月律以奏，及進膳、迎膳等曲，皆用樂府、小令、雜劇爲娛戲。

translations.literal: The twelve-month songs were performed by monthly pitch; pieces for presenting and welcoming the feast used yuefu, short songs, and variety drama for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve-month songs followed the monthly pitch; presenting and welcoming the feast relied on yuefu, short songs, and variety plays for amusement.

sentences.zh: 流俗喧嘵，淫哇不逞。

translations.literal: Vulgar clamor and unrestrained sensual sound prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Popular noise and unrestrained sensual sound prevailed.

sentences.zh: 太祖所欲屏者，顧反設之殿陛間不爲怪也。

translations.literal: What the founder wished to banish was instead set before the throne without occasion for surprise.
translations.idiomatic: What the founder had meant to exclude was now installed on the palace steps as if it were nothing strange.

sentences.zh: 永樂十八年，北京郊廟成。

translations.literal: In Yongle year 18 the Beijing suburban temples were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Yongle the Beijing suburban temples were completed.

sentences.zh: 其合祀合享禮樂，一如舊制。

translations.literal: Combined sacrifice and combined offering rites and music followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Combined sacrifice and combined offering followed the old regulations in every respect.

sentences.zh: 更定宴饗樂舞：初奏《上萬壽之曲》，《平定天下之舞》；

translations.literal: Banquet music and dance were revised: first *Shang wanshou zhi qu* with *Pingding tianxia zhi wu*;
translations.idiomatic: Banquet music and dance were revised: first *Ten Thousand Years to Your Majesty* with *Pacifying the Realm Under Heaven*;

sentences.zh: 二奏《仰天恩之曲》，《撫四夷之舞》；

translations.literal: second *Yang tian'en zhi qu* with *Fu siyi zhi wu*;
translations.idiomatic: second *Looking Up to Heaven's Grace* with *Pacifying the Four Barbarians*;

sentences.zh: 三奏《感地德之曲》，《車書會同之舞》；

translations.literal: third *Gan dide zhi qu* with *Cheshu huitong zhi wu*;
translations.idiomatic: third *Grateful for Earth's Virtue* with *Chariots and Script Unite*;

sentences.zh: 四奏《民樂生之曲》，《表正萬邦之舞》；

translations.literal: fourth *Min lesheng zhi qu* with *Biaozheng wanbang zhi wu*;
translations.idiomatic: fourth *The People Find Life* with *Setting Right the Myriad States*;

sentences.zh: 五奏《感皇恩之曲》，《天命有德之舞》；

translations.literal: fifth *Gan huang'en zhi qu* with *Tianming youde zhi wu*;
translations.idiomatic: fifth *Grateful for Imperial Grace* with *Heaven's Mandate Has Virtue*;

sentences.zh: 六奏《慶豐年之曲》；

translations.literal: sixth *Qing fengnian zhi qu*;
translations.idiomatic: sixth *Celebrating a Bountiful Year*;

sentences.zh: 七奏《集禎應之曲》；

translations.literal: seventh *Ji zhenying zhi qu*;
translations.idiomatic: seventh *Gathering Auspicious Responses*;

sentences.zh: 八奏《永皇圖之曲》；

translations.literal: eighth *Yong huangtu zhi qu*;
translations.idiomatic: eighth *Forever the Imperial Domain*;

sentences.zh: 九奏《樂太平之曲》。

translations.literal: ninth *Le taiping zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: ninth *Rejoicing in Great Peace*.

sentences.zh: 奏曲膚淺，舞曲益下俚。

translations.literal: The melodies were shallow; the dances still more vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: The songs were shallow; the dances cruder still.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，助教劉翔上書指其失。

translations.literal: In Jingtai year 1 Assistant Instructor Liu Xiang memorialized pointing out the faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingtai, Assistant Instructor Liu Xiang submitted a memorial on these faults.

sentences.zh: 請敕儒臣推演道德教化之意，君臣相與之樂，作爲詩章，協以律呂，如古《靈臺》、《辟雍》、《清廟》、《湛露》之音，以振勵風教，備一代盛典。

translations.literal: He asked that Confucian officials be ordered to develop the meaning of moral teaching, compose poetry for the joy shared between ruler and minister, harmonize it to pitch and mode like the ancient *Lingtai*, *Piyong*, *Qingmiao*, and *Zhanlu* pieces, to revive custom and complete a generation's great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that scholar-officials be charged to draw on moral teaching, compose verses for the joy of ruler and minister, and set them to pitch and mode like the ancient *Ling Terrace*, *Academy*, *Clear Temple*, and *Heavy Dew*—to revive custom and crown the age.

sentences.zh: 時以襲用既久，卒莫能改。

translations.literal: Because usage was long entrenched, in the end nothing could be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Long usage had hardened into habit, and in the end nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 其後教坊司樂工所奏中和韶樂，且多不諧者。

translations.literal: Later the Shao music performed by Instruction Office musicians was often out of tune.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Shao music of the Instruction Office was often out of tune.

sentences.zh: 成化中，禮官嘗請三倍其額，博教而約取之。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign ritual officials once asked to triple the quota, teach broadly, and select narrowly.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua the ritual officials once proposed tripling the roster, teaching widely, and selecting strictly.

sentences.zh: 弘治之初，孝宗親耕耤田，教坊司以雜劇承應，間出狎語。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi, when Xiaozong personally plowed the sacred field, the Instruction Office supplied variety drama and occasionally let coarse jokes slip.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi, when Xiaozong plowed the sacred field himself, the Instruction Office supplied variety plays and sometimes let coarse jokes slip.

sentences.zh: 都御史馬文升厲色斥去。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Ma Wensheng sternly rebuked them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Ma Wensheng rebuked them sharply and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡瑞嘗言：「御殿受朝，典禮至大，而殿中中和韶樂乃屬之教坊司，嶽鎮海瀆，三年一祭，乃委之神樂觀樂舞生，褻神明，傷大體。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Hu Rui once said: "Receiving audience in the imperial hall is a ceremony of the utmost weight, yet hall Shao music belongs to the Instruction Office; the peaks, seas, and rivers are sacrificed once every three years yet entrusted to music students of the Divine Music Office—this profanes the spirits and wounds great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Hu Rui once said: "Audience in the imperial hall is the weightiest ceremony, yet hall Shao music is left to the Instruction Office; the sacred mountains and rivers are sacrificed only every three years yet left to Divine Music Office students—profaning the spirits and wounding the state's dignity.

sentences.zh: 望敕廷臣議，嶽瀆等祭，當以縉紳從事。

translations.literal: He hoped the emperor would order court officials to deliberate: sacrifices to the peaks and rivers should be conducted by gentry-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the throne order court officials to debate whether sacrifices to the sacred mountains and rivers ought to be performed by gentry-officials.

sentences.zh: 中和韶樂，擇民間子弟肆習，設官掌之。

translations.literal: Shao music should select commoners' sons for training and establish officials to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao music should be taught to sons of common families under appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 年久則量授職事。

translations.literal: After long service they should be granted posts in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: After long service they should receive offices in due measure.

sentences.zh: 」帝以奏樂遣祭，皆國朝舊典，不能從也。

translations.literal: " The emperor held that sending musicians to perform sacrifices was an old statute of the dynasty and could not be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that using musicians at sacrifices was an old dynastic statute and could not be changed.

sentences.zh: 馬文升爲尚書，因災異陳言，其一訪名儒以正雅樂，事下禮官。

translations.literal: Ma Wensheng became Minister and, citing omens and disasters, submitted advice; one item was to seek renowned scholars to rectify elegant music, and the matter was sent to the ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Wensheng became Minister he cited omens in memorial, among them seeking renowned scholars to rectify court music; the matter went to the ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「高皇帝命儒臣考定八音，修造樂器，參定樂章。

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: "The founding emperor ordered Confucian officials to examine and fix the eight sounds, repair and make instruments, and collate hymn texts.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials replied: "The founding emperor ordered scholars to fix the eight sounds, repair instruments, and collate hymn texts.

sentences.zh: 其登歌之詞，多自裁定。

translations.literal: The words for elevated singing were largely set by his own decision.
translations.idiomatic: The elevated-singing texts were largely his own composition.

sentences.zh: 但歷今百三十餘年，不復校正，音律舛訛，釐正宜急。

translations.literal: But more than one hundred thirty years have passed without correction; pitch and mode are awry, and rectification is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet more than one hundred thirty years have passed without revision; pitches are wrong and correction is urgent.

sentences.zh: 且太常官恐未足當制器協律之任。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials may not suffice for the task of making instruments and harmonizing pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Court of Imperial Sacrifices officers may not suffice to make instruments and harmonize pitch.

sentences.zh: 乞詔下諸司，博求中外臣工及山林有精曉音律者，禮送京師。

translations.literal: We beg an edict to all offices to seek broadly among inner and outer officials and among recluses in mountains and forests who understand pitch well, and send them to the capital with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: We beg an edict commanding all offices to seek, at court and in the hills, those who understand pitch, and ceremonially send them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會禮官熟議至當，然後造器正音，庶幾可以復祖制，致太和。

translations.literal: When ritual officials have deliberated to satisfaction, then make instruments and correct pitch—perhaps the ancestral system may be restored and great harmony attained."
translations.idiomatic: When ritual officials have agreed on the right course, instruments may be made and pitch corrected—perhaps the ancestral system and great harmony may be restored."

sentences.zh: 」帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 末年詔南京及各王府，選精通樂藝者詣京師，復以禮官言而罷。

translations.literal: In his later years he ordered Nanjing and each princely establishment to select those skilled in music and send them to the capital; again, on the ritual officials' word, this was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Late in his reign he ordered Nanjing and the princely establishments to send skilled musicians to the capital, but on the ritual officials' advice the order was dropped.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，武宗諭內鐘鼓司康能等曰：「慶成大宴，華夷臣工所觀瞻，宜舉大樂。

translations.literal: In Zhengde year 3 the Martial Emperor instructed Kang Neng and others of the inner Bell-and-Drum Office: "The celebration banquet after great felicity is watched by Chinese and barbarian officials; great music ought to be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 3 the Martial Emperor told Kang Neng of the inner Bell-and-Drum Office: "The post-celebration banquet is watched by court and foreign officials alike; the court should perform great music.

sentences.zh: 邇者音樂廢缺，無以重朝廷。

translations.literal: " Recently music has fallen into ruin and lacks what is needed to dignify the court.
translations.idiomatic: Of late music has decayed and no longer dignifies the court."

sentences.zh: 」禮部乃請選三院樂工年壯者，嚴督肄之，仍移各省司取藝精者赴京供應。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of Rites then asked to select young musicians from the three academies for strict training, and also to summon the most skilled from provincial offices to the capital for service.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites then proposed selecting young musicians from the three academies for strict training and summoning the finest from the provinces to serve at court.

sentences.zh: 顧所隸益猥雜，筋斗百戲之類日盛于禁廷。

translations.literal: Yet those subordinate to them grew ever more vulgar and mixed; tumbling and variety acts daily flourished in the forbidden palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their ranks grew ever more vulgar; tumbling and variety acts flourished daily in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 既而河間等府奉詔送樂戶，居之新宅。

translations.literal: Before long musicians from Hejian and other prefectures were sent by imperial order and housed in new residences.
translations.idiomatic: Soon musicians from Hejian and other prefectures arrived by imperial order and were lodged in new quarters.

sentences.zh: 樂工既得幸，時時言居外者不宜獨逸，乃復移各省司所送技精者於教坊。

translations.literal: Once favored, the musicians often said those outside should not alone enjoy ease, and so the skilled sent from provincial offices were again moved to the Instruction Office.
translations.idiomatic: Favored, the musicians complained that those outside should not enjoy ease alone, and skilled men sent from the provinces were moved again to the Instruction Office.

sentences.zh: 於是乘傳續食者又數百人，俳優之勢大張。

translations.literal: Then several hundred more traveled on relay rations; the power of actors swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds more traveled on relay rations, and the actors' influence swelled.

sentences.zh: 臧賢以伶人進，與諸佞幸角寵竊權矣。

translations.literal: Zang Xian entered as an actor and vied with other favorites for favor and stolen power.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xian rose as an actor and contended with other favorites for influence.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，御史汪珊請屏絕玩好，令教坊司毋得以新聲巧技進。

translations.literal: In Jiajing year 1 Censor Wang Shan asked to banish frivolous delights and forbid the Instruction Office from presenting new sounds and clever tricks.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 1 Censor Wang Shan asked to banish frivolous delights and forbid the Instruction Office new sounds and clever tricks.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 是時更定諸典禮，因亦有志於樂。

translations.literal: At that time various ceremonies were being revised, and he also turned his mind to music.
translations.idiomatic: As rites were being revised across the board, he also turned to music.

sentences.zh: 建觀德殿以祀獻帝，如協律郎肄樂供祀事。

translations.literal: The Observing Virtue Hall was built to sacrifice to the deceased emperor, with pitch-regulation officers drilling music for the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Observing Virtue Hall was built to honor the deceased emperor, with pitch officers drilling music for its rites.

sentences.zh: 後建世廟成，改殿曰崇先。

translations.literal: Later, when the World Temple was completed, the hall was renamed Honoring the Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: When the World Temple was completed the hall was renamed Honoring the Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 乃親制樂章，命大學士費宏等更定曲名，以別於太廟。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed hymn texts and ordered Grand Secretaries Fei Hong and others to revise tune names to distinguish them from the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He personally composed hymns and ordered Grand Secretaries Fei Hong and others to rename the tunes, distinct from the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 其迎神曰《永和之曲》。

translations.literal: For welcoming the spirit: *Yonghe zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: Welcoming the spirit: *Everlasting Harmony*.

sentences.zh: 初獻曰《清和之曲》，亞獻曰《康和之曲》，終獻曰《沖和之曲》，徹饌曰《泰和之曲》，送神曰《寧和之曲》。

translations.literal: First offering *Qinghe zhi qu*, second offering *Kanghe zhi qu*, final offering *Chonghe zhi qu*, clearing the feast *Taihe zhi qu*, sending off the spirit *Ninghe zhi qu*.
translations.idiomatic: First offering *Pure Harmony*, second *Abundant Harmony*, final *Pervading Harmony*, clearing the feast *Supreme Harmony*, sending off the spirit *Tranquil Harmony*.

sentences.zh: 宏等復議，獻皇生長太平，不尚武功，其三獻皆當用《文德舞》。

translations.literal: Hong and others further argued that the deceased emperor had grown up in peace and did not esteem martial display; all three offerings should use the *Civil Virtue Dance*.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Hong argued that the deceased emperor, raised in peace, did not favor martial display and that all three offerings should use the Civil Virtue Dance.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而太常復請，乃命禮官會張璁議。

translations.literal: Later the Court of Imperial Sacrifices again petitioned, and the emperor ordered ritual officials to meet with Zhang Cong.
